question: A team is defining multidimensional success criteria for a Claude-based assistant that drafts customer refund emails using data from a live order-management system. Which of the following are appropriate success-criteria categories to include in the evaluation, based on evaluation design best practices? (Select all that apply.)
options: A) Model parameter count, measuring how many parameters the underlying model has relative to competing models
B) Privacy preservation, measuring whether the email avoids exposing another customer's order or payment information
C) Raw token count of each generated email, tracked independently of any cost or response-time target
D) Training data volume, measuring how many examples of refund emails were used to pretrain the underlying model
E) Consistency, measuring whether semantically similar refund scenarios produce similarly structured emails
F) Task fidelity, measuring whether the drafted email correctly reflects the order and refund details from the system
correct_answers: B) Privacy preservation, measuring whether the email avoids exposing another customer's order or payment information
E) Consistency, measuring whether semantically similar refund scenarios produce similarly structured emails
F) Task fidelity, measuring whether the drafted email correctly reflects the order and refund details from the system
explanations: Incorrect. Parameter count is an internal model property, not an output-quality success criterion the evaluation dataset can meaningfully score.
Correct. Privacy preservation is a standard success-criteria category, and it is directly relevant here since the assistant handles other customers' order and payment data.
Incorrect. Raw token count in isolation, without tying it to a cost or latency target, is not one of the recognized success-criteria categories.
Incorrect. Pretraining data volume is a model-development detail unrelated to measuring the quality of this specific feature's outputs.
Correct. Consistency, ensuring similar inputs produce similarly structured outputs, is a standard success-criteria category and is meaningful for a template-like task like refund emails.
Correct. Task fidelity, measuring accuracy on the core task, is a standard success-criteria category directly applicable to whether the drafted email reflects the correct order and refund data.
